content.title: Eid al-Fitr 2026: Is it a holiday today in the US? Are schools and offices open across America?
content.text: Eid al-Fitr 2026: As Muslims across the United States greet one another with “Eid Mubarak” and celebrate the end of Ramadan, a common question remains: Is it a holiday today in the US?Eid al-Fitr 2026, which falls on March 20 in several countries and March 21 in parts of South Asia, is not a federal public holiday in the United States. This means that government offices, banks, and most private businesses continue to function as usual.However, the absence of official holiday status has not diminished the scale of celebrations. Increasingly, workplaces and educational institutions are offering flexibility, allowing employees and students to take leave to observe the festival. For many Muslim families, the day is marked by early morning prayers, festive meals, and community gatherings, even if it is not formally recognised nationwide as a day off.Are schools, colleges and offices open?Since Eid is not a federal holiday, most schools, colleges, and offices remain open across the country. Yet, the ground reality reflects a growing cultural shift.Several school districts, particularly in states with significant Muslim populations, have declared Eid al-Fitr as an official holiday. These include New York City public schools, parts of New Jersey, Michigan, Texas, and Maryland. In such regions, students enjoy a day off, aligning with the spirit of the festival, as per a report by Indian Eagle.In workplaces, employers are increasingly accommodating religious diversity. Many Muslim employees apply for leave or adjust schedules to attend prayers and spend time with family. Universities, too, often provide academic flexibility, recognising Eid as an important religious observance.How Eid Mubarak is being celebrated in the USDespite not being a nationwide holiday today, Eid celebrations across the US are vibrant and deeply rooted in tradition.The day typically begins with special congregational prayers held at mosques, convention centres, parks, and open grounds. Worshippers gather early in the morning, recite prayers, and exchange greetings of “happy eid” and “Eid Mubarak.”Charity remains central to the festival. Muslims offer Zakat al-Fitr, ensuring that those in need can also partake in the celebrations. This act underscores the values of compassion and community.Following prayers, families come together for elaborate meals, often featuring traditional dishes such as biryani, kebabs, and sweet delicacies like seviyan. Children receive gifts and “Eidi,” while relatives and friends visit one another, strengthening social bonds.Community events, fairs, and cultural programmes are also organised in cities with large Muslim populations, blending religious observance with festive cheer.Eid Al-Fitr: Retail buzz and Eid offers gain momentumEid is also emerging as a key seasonal moment for businesses in the US. With rising digital engagement and cross-border connections, brands have begun rolling out targeted promotions.Financial service platforms are offering zero-fee remittance deals, enabling families to send money abroad during the festive period. Meanwhile, online retail and education platforms have introduced Eid-themed discounts, tapping into the celebratory spending mood.These campaigns highlight how Eid, while not an official holiday today, is increasingly influencing consumer trends in the American market.Cities where Eid celebrations are most prominentEid al-Fitr is celebrated across the US, but certain states and cities stand out for their large-scale observances.New York, California, Illinois, New Jersey, Texas, and Michigan host some of the biggest gatherings, reflecting their sizeable Muslim populations. Cities like New York City and Dearborn in Michigan are known for expansive Eid prayers and community festivals.Public recognition has also grown steadily. While the White House continues the tradition of extending Eid greetings, several state governments and city administrations issue official proclamations acknowledging the festival.Eid Al-Fitr: Holiday today? Growing recognition but no federal holiday statusAlthough Eid al-Fitr has not yet been declared a federal holiday, its visibility and recognition continue to expand. States like Washington have formally included Eid in their calendars, while others have passed legislation enabling schools to observe the festival.This gradual shift reflects the increasing cultural and social significance of Eid in the US, driven by a diverse and growing Muslim population.
